transfer.action.HELD_BY_DIRECTION: held back by the sync direction
sessions.scope.title: Working set
sessions.scope.caption: Pick what this machine should carry. Only writes into .codex are narrowed: the cloud mirror always receives every session, so the backup is never partial.

sessions.scope.not_in_catalog.one: {count} chat in the set cannot be written into .codex yet: this machine's thread catalogue does not place it, and codexSync does not write that row. It is still mirrored to the cloud.
sessions.scope.not_in_catalog.other: {count} chats in the set cannot be written into .codex yet: this machine's thread catalogue does not place them, and codexSync does not write those rows. They are still mirrored to the cloud.

settings.mapping.form.title: Rule

settings.mapping.reach.one: This folder is named by {count} chat on this machine.
settings.mapping.reach.other: This folder is named by {count} chats on this machine.

settings.mapping.hint.rule_id: Any name that says what the rule is for; it only has to be unique.
settings.mapping.hint.source_machine: The machine the recorded path came from.
settings.mapping.hint.target_machine: The machine the path is translated for — usually this one.
settings.mapping.hint.from: The folder as the other machine wrote it. The list offers folders chats name that do not exist here.
settings.mapping.hint.to: The same folder on this machine.
settings.mapping.hint.case_sensitive: Auto follows the operating system: Windows and macOS ignore case, Linux does not.
no_config.title: No configuration is open
no_config.detail: This page works on a config.toml. Open the one you already have — it can live in any folder — or create a new one where you choose.
page.overview.subtitle: A manual check of this machine. It does not authorise any write.
page.first_run.subtitle: Create config.toml, name this machine, and choose the local .codex and the synced workspace.
page.sync.subtitle: The cloud → local and local → cloud plan. Checking the plan writes nothing.
page.chats.subtitle: Which project each chat is under, and why. This is not a chat window.
page.sessions.subtitle: How each branch of a session compares across two machines. Divergent histories are never merged.
page.projects.subtitle: Projects, their roots, and repairing bindings after moving to another machine.
page.guardian.subtitle: Verified snapshots of .codex-global-state.json, taken outside .codex.
page.backups.subtitle: Verified backups and restoring from them. A restore starts with a dry run.
page.recovery.subtitle: An unfinished journal blocks every new change until it is resumed or rolled back.
page.settings.subtitle: Settings that change what CodexSync does are stored in config.toml.
page.about.subtitle: What this program is, what it refuses to do, and which build you are running.
settings.roots.hint: What is ticked here is written into the box as a list of roots. A folder covers everything inside it. Files holding credentials are not listed at all, and paths the semantic layer owns cannot be ticked — plain sync never copies them.
settings.roots.semantic: sessions and state: moved by their own commands, not by sync
machines.required: Name both machines: the one the sessions were recorded on and this one.
failure.codex-not-stopped: Codex is open, or its state could not be determined
failure.needs-a-decision: This needs a decision only you can make
failure.stopped-safely: The operation stopped without changing anything
failure.unexpected: Something went wrong that should not have
failure.code.CONFIG_OUTDATED: this config was written by an earlier version of codexSync. Update it in Settings with ‘Update the config’: your values and comments are kept.
failure.code.CHAT_DECISIONS_NEEDED: some chats exist on both machines in different versions and need your decision; nothing was written. Open Sessions to decide, then synchronise again.
failure.code.RECOVERY_PENDING: an earlier operation stopped half-way and its journal is still open, so nothing was changed. It needs a decision on the Recovery page.
banner.config.outdated: This config was written by an earlier version of codexSync, and with it sync, chat transfer and restore write nothing. Update it: your values and comments are kept, and the old file goes to the config history.
banner.config.differs: Some settings in this config are written differently by this version. See what would change and update it.
banner.stopped.title: Codex is probably closed
banner.stopped.detail: Changes will still check this again immediately before writing.
banner.running.title: Codex is open, or its state could not be determined
banner.running.detail: Changes are refused until Codex is closed. An undetermined state is never treated as closed.
checks.title: Environment checks
dry_run.caption: It builds and checks the plan, but copies and writes nothing.
dry_run.done: Dry run finished. Nothing was copied or written.
sync.caption: Checking the plan writes nothing and works while Codex is open. The dry run and the sync need Codex closed; the sync builds its plan again at the moment it writes, so what is on screen is never what gets applied.
sync.not_checked: The plan has not been built yet.
sync.nothing: Both sides agree: nothing to copy.
sync.plan.title: Plan
sync.filter.nothing_shown: Nothing matches the search. The plan itself is unchanged.
sync.filter.whole_plan: The search and the filters change what is shown here. Synchronise applies the whole plan: sync has no partial apply.
sync.volatile.title: Codex is open, so this plan is only a preview
sync.volatile.detail: Files may still change. Close Codex before the dry run or the sync; both rebuild the plan anyway.
sync.conflicts.title: Some files changed on both sides
sync.conflicts.detail: With the manual_abort policy the sync stops before writing anything. Resolve those files by hand or change the conflict policy in Settings.
sync.confirm.title: Synchronise now?
sync.confirm.body: Codex must be closed. Settings, chats and projects are synced in both directions: the plan is built again right now, everything that would be replaced is backed up first, and the process check is repeated before each replace. Nothing is deleted.
sync.done.dry: Dry run finished. Nothing was copied or written.
sync.history.caption: Every run that wrote something — Synchronise from this window, the command line, a task or another page. One full sync is three rows: settings files, chats and projects. Dry runs write nothing and are not listed, and neither is a run that stopped before its first write (Codex open, a conflict under manual_abort). Read from the same operation journals as the Recovery page.
sync.history.failure.Abandoned: interrupted before anything was replaced; closed by the next run
sync.decisions.title: Synchronisation stopped before writing anything: some chats exist on both machines in different versions, and only you can decide which to keep.
sync.decisions.next: Choose below which copies to keep, for all of them at once: the copy not kept is saved whole first. Or open Sessions to decide one by one.
sync.decide.remember: Always decide this way (saved as the conflict policy in Settings)
sync.decide.confirm.title: Synchronise again
sync.decide.confirm.prefer_newer_mtime: Synchronise again, keeping whichever copy is newer: a chat by its last message, a settings file by its modification time. Codex must be closed. The copy not kept is saved first: a chat whole in the conflict bundle, a file in the backup. Chats that end at the same moment are still asked about.
sync.decide.confirm.prefer_local: Synchronise again, keeping this machine's copy of everything changed on both machines. Codex must be closed. The cloud's copy is saved first: a chat whole in the conflict bundle, a file in the backup.
sync.decide.confirm.prefer_cloud: Synchronise again, keeping the cloud's copy of everything changed on both machines. Codex must be closed. This machine's copy is saved first: a chat whole in the conflict bundle, a file in the backup.
sync.decide.confirm.remember: The rule is also saved as the conflict policy, so every later sync (window, console, sign-in task) decides the same way.

sync.decisions.format_migrations.one: {count} chat was only rewritten by Codex into its newer format — safe to accept at once
sync.decisions.format_migrations.other: {count} chats were only rewritten by Codex into its newer format — safe to accept at once

sync.decisions.held_migrations.one: {count} chat in the older format has later messages — check it before choosing
sync.decisions.held_migrations.other: {count} chats in the older format have later messages — check them before choosing

sync.decisions.divergences.one: {count} chat was continued differently on the two machines
sync.decisions.divergences.other: {count} chats were continued differently on the two machines

sync.decisions.collisions.one: {count} chat would land on a file that already exists here
sync.decisions.collisions.other: {count} chats would land on files that already exist here

sync.note.missing_folders.one: {count} added project has no folder on this machine: create the folder or add a path mapping.
sync.note.missing_folders.other: {count} added projects have no folder on this machine: create the folders or add a path mapping.

sync.note.chats_not_loaded.one: {count} chat stayed in the cloud copy only; the Sessions page shows why.
sync.note.chats_not_loaded.other: {count} chats stayed in the cloud copy only; the Sessions page shows why.

sync.note.codex_will_list.one: Codex will show {count} chat after its next start: it rebuilds its chat list from the files, so that start takes longer.
sync.note.codex_will_list.other: Codex will show {count} chats after its next start: it rebuilds its chat list from the files, so that start takes longer.

sync.note.decided_by_rule.one: {count} chat had changed on both machines and was decided by the conflict policy; the copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle.
sync.note.decided_by_rule.other: {count} chats had changed on both machines and were decided by the conflict policy; each copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle.

sync.note.names_set.one: {count} chat got its name from the other machine.
sync.note.names_set.other: {count} chats got their names from the other machine.

sync.note.names_waiting.one: {count} chat gets its name on the next sync, once Codex lists it.
sync.note.names_waiting.other: {count} chats get their names on the next sync, once Codex lists them.

sync.note.names_kept.one: {count} chat is named differently on the other machine; the name here was kept.
sync.note.names_kept.other: {count} chats are named differently on the other machine; the names here were kept.

sync.note.files.BEHIND: Project {project}: the last commit from {machine} is not here. Pull it before continuing its chats.
sync.note.files.DIVERGED: Project {project}: here and on {machine} different commits were made. Merge them before continuing its chats.
sync.note.files.UNCOMMITTED_THERE: Project {project}: {machine} has changes that were not committed and are not here.
sync.note.files.FILES_CHANGED_THERE: Project {project}: on {machine}, {newer} file(s) changed later, {missing} exist only there and {removed} were deleted there. Bring them over before continuing its chats.
sync.note.files.chats_there: Chats of this project went on there until {when}.
sync.note.files.MISSING_HERE: Project {project}: its folder does not exist on this machine.

sync.note.codex_ignores.one: Codex still does not list {count} chat file after rebuilding its chat list. The file is in place and nothing was lost.
sync.note.codex_ignores.other: Codex still does not list {count} chat files after rebuilding its chat list. The files are in place and nothing was lost.

sync.note.new_chats_in_cloud.one: {count} chat new to this machine stayed in the cloud copy: loading new chats is off (Settings → Synchronisation → “New chats from another machine”).
sync.note.new_chats_in_cloud.other: {count} chats new to this machine stayed in the cloud copy: loading new chats is off (Settings → Synchronisation → “New chats from another machine”).

chats.search: Search the opening message or the folder
chats.source_machine.tip: Name the machine the chats were recorded on to apply [[path_mappings]] rules from it to this machine.
chats.tree.title: Chats by project
chats.column.title: Chat
chats.volatile.title: Codex is open
chats.volatile.detail: A chat open right now is still being written. Moving chats needs Codex closed.

chats.stranded.title.one: {count} chat is reachable only through a mapping rule
chats.stranded.title.other: {count} chats are reachable only through a mapping rule

chats.stranded.detail: Codex does not read [[path_mappings]], so it shows these chats under no project until they are pinned. Auto-repair below proposes exactly those pins.
chats.move.title: Move chats to a project
chats.move.nothing: Nothing to write: every chat named is already under that project.

chats.move.ready.one: Ready: {count} binding to write. The id covers the current state, so it stops matching if anything changes.
chats.move.ready.other: Ready: {count} bindings to write. The id covers the current state, so it stops matching if anything changes.

chats.move.confirm.title: Move these chats?
chats.move.confirm.body: {count} binding(s) will be written for plan {plan_id}. Codex must be closed; the global state is backed up first and restored if anything fails.

chats.move.done.dry.one: Dry run finished: {count} binding would be written. Nothing was written.
chats.move.done.dry.other: Dry run finished: {count} bindings would be written. Nothing was written.

chats.autofix.label: Auto-repair
chats.autofix.note: Only unambiguous links are proposed: chats a mapping rule connects to exactly one project. Everything else stays a manual choice.
sessions.caption: Scanning reads both sides and writes only the plan file. It works while Codex is open, but such a plan is marked volatile and cannot be applied.
sessions.scanning: Comparing branches… this reads every session file and can take a while.
sessions.branches.title: Branches
sessions.scope.counting: Working out what the set covers…
sessions.records.tip: Records in this machine's branch / in the cloud mirror's branch
sessions.volatile.title: Codex is open: this plan cannot be applied
sessions.volatile.detail: Close Codex and scan again before applying.
sessions.decide.detail: A divergence is never merged. Decide them all at once by one rule, or select one and choose which side to keep; the scan is repeated with your decision.
sessions.clean.title: Nothing needs a decision
sessions.partial.title: Not everything is carried

sessions.note.new_in_cloud.one: {count} chat exists only on the other machine and stays in the cloud copy: loading new chats onto this machine is off. To turn it on: Settings → Synchronisation → “New chats from another machine” → “copy into .codex”.
sessions.note.new_in_cloud.other: {count} chats exist only on the other machine and stay in the cloud copy: loading new chats onto this machine is off. To turn it on: Settings → Synchronisation → “New chats from another machine” → “copy into .codex”.

sessions.note.held.one: {count} chat is not brought here: Codex on this machine does not confirm where its file is (the row's tooltip says why).
sessions.note.held.other: {count} chats are not brought here: Codex on this machine does not confirm where their files are (each row's tooltip says why).

sessions.note.unreadable.one: {count} chat is not carried: a copy cannot be read, or the chat sits in several files.
sessions.note.unreadable.other: {count} chats are not carried: a copy cannot be read, or the chat sits in several files.

sessions.note.moves.one: {count} chat will be archived or unarchived, as on the other machine.
sessions.note.moves.other: {count} chats will be archived or unarchived, as on the other machine.

sessions.note.stale.one: {count} chat sits in two files here: the one Codex names is carried, the other is left alone.
sessions.note.stale.other: {count} chats sit in two files here: the one Codex names is carried, the other is left alone.

sessions.note.decided.one: {count} chat changed on both machines is decided by the conflict rule; the copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle.
sessions.note.decided.other: {count} chats changed on both machines are decided by the conflict rule; each copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle.

sessions.note.direction.one: {count} chat is not written: the sync direction is one-way.
sessions.note.direction.other: {count} chats are not written: the sync direction is one-way.

sessions.choice.label: Decision for the selected conflict
sessions.rule.label: All conflicts at once:
sessions.resolve.hint: Conflict {conflict_id}…: the decision is pinned to the exact bytes of both branches. The losing branch is kept in a conflict bundle.
sessions.resolve.select: Select a branch that needs a decision to record one.
sessions.resolved: Decision recorded; the plan was rebuilt with it.
sessions.format.resolve: Keep the new format for all

sessions.format.hint.one: {count} conflict is only Codex rewriting a chat into its newer record format. One decision keeps the new copy for all of them; each old copy is kept, compressed.
sessions.format.hint.other: {count} conflicts are only Codex rewriting chats into its newer record format. One decision keeps the new copy for all of them; each old copy is kept, compressed.

sessions.format.held.one: {count} more needs a decision of its own: its old copy has a record later than the new one.
sessions.format.held.other: {count} more need a decision of their own: the old copy has a record later than the new one.

sessions.plan.title: Plan

sessions.plan.cwd_absent.one: {count} chat bound for .codex has no working folder on this machine — a working set can leave it out
sessions.plan.cwd_absent.other: {count} chats bound for .codex have no working folder on this machine — a working set can leave them out

sessions.confirm.title: Apply the session plan?
sessions.confirm.body: {count} branch(es) will be written for plan {plan_id}. Codex must be closed. The plan is rebuilt first and refused if its id no longer matches; everything replaced is backed up.

sessions.confirm.decided.one: {count} of them changed on both machines; the copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle first.
sessions.confirm.decided.other: {count} of them changed on both machines; each copy not kept is saved whole in the conflict bundle first.

sessions.done.dry.one: Dry run finished: {count} branch would be written. Nothing was written.
sessions.done.dry.other: Dry run finished: {count} branches would be written. Nothing was written.

projects.list.title: Projects
projects.list.caption: Chats per project by the reason they are there. Chats found only by a mapping rule are invisible in Codex until pinned.
projects.column.name: Project
projects.lost.detail: Pin them from Chat bindings, or build the repair plan below.
sync.note.files.MISSING_THERE: Project {project}: its folder exists here but not on {machine}.
projects.files.title: Project folders
projects.files.caption: Chats travel between machines, project folders do not. Every start, full sync and check reads the folders afresh and compares them with what the other machines last published. Nothing is copied or changed.
projects.files.none_published: No other machine has published its project folders yet; it does on its next start or sync.
projects.files.verdict.BEHIND: the last commit from there is not here

projects.files.all_here.one: {count} project folder holds what the other machines had.
projects.files.all_here.other: All {count} project folders hold what the other machines had.

projects.files.attention.one: {count} project did not fully come along.
projects.files.attention.other: {count} projects did not fully come along.

projects.repair.title: Repair after moving to another machine
projects.repair.caption: Sessions' recorded folders are run through [[path_mappings]]. The plan pins chats, or remaps a moved project's root — and a remap always also pins every chat still under the old root, so none of them disappears.
projects.repair.volatile: Codex is open: this plan is a preview and cannot be applied. Close Codex and build it again.
projects.repair.confirm.title: Apply the repair plan?
projects.repair.confirm.body: {count} change(s) will be written to the global state for plan {plan_id}. Codex must be closed; a full backup is made first and restored if validation fails. Session files are never rewritten.

projects.repair.done.dry.one: Dry run finished: {count} change would be applied. Nothing was written.
projects.repair.done.dry.other: Dry run finished: {count} changes would be applied. Nothing was written.

projects.move.title: Moving a project to another folder
projects.move.body: Copies the project into a folder that does not exist yet, verifies every file, then points Codex at it and pins the chats that reached it by path. The old folder is never modified or deleted. Session histories are never rewritten.
repair.kind.SKIP_NO_PROJECT: no project here — create it in Codex
guardian.taking: Reading the state until it is stable…
guardian.caption: Allowed while Codex is open: the state is only read, and the snapshot is written outside .codex, the mirror, backups and temp.
guardian.latest.title: Latest good snapshot: {created}
guardian.latest.none: There is no verified snapshot to restore from
guardian.snapshots.title: Snapshots
guardian.quarantine.title: Quarantine
guardian.quarantine.caption: States Guardian refused to trust, with the reason. None of them can ever become the latest good snapshot.
guardian.result.UNCHANGED: The state has not changed since the last snapshot.
guardian.result.QUARANTINED: The state failed validation and went to quarantine.
guardian.result.BUSY: Another Guardian is writing right now; skipped.
guardian.reason.BROKEN_ORDER_REFERENCE: project order names a missing project
guardian.reason.READ_CHANGED: the file kept changing while read
backups.list.title: Backups
backups.column.name: Name
backups.restore.title: Restore
backups.restore.caption: A dry run verifies every file against the manifest and plans the copy without writing. The restore itself needs Codex closed and backs up whatever it replaces first.
backups.copies.caption: A full copy of what matters in .codex — chats, projects, catalogues, settings, never secrets — as one zip file. Taken only while Codex is closed; putting one back is done by hand.
backups.copies.no_folder: No folder is chosen for copies, so they are off. Choose one under Automation → Copies of .codex.
backups.not_restorable: This backup has no verified manifest and cannot be restored here.
backups.dry_first: Run the dry run for this backup and target first; the restore button unlocks after it succeeds.
backups.confirm.title: Restore this backup?
backups.confirm.body: {name} will be restored into {target}. Codex must be closed; every file it replaces is backed up first.

backups.done.dry.one: Dry run finished: {count} file from {name} would be restored. Nothing was written.
backups.done.dry.other: Dry run finished: {count} files from {name} would be restored. Nothing was written.

recovery.blocked.detail: Look at the evidence, then either resume (close the journal and re-run the command) or roll back into an explicitly chosen target.

recovery.self_closing.title.one: {count} interrupted operation will close by itself
recovery.self_closing.title.other: {count} interrupted operations will close by themselves

recovery.self_closing.detail: They stopped before replacing anything. The next synchronisation on this machine closes them; you can also close them here now.
recovery.clear.title: No interrupted operation
recovery.list.title: Mutation journals
recovery.actions.title: What can be done
recovery.select: Select a journal to see its evidence.
recovery.evidence.closed: This journal is closed ({state}); there is nothing to recover.
recovery.evidence.unreadable: This journal cannot be read. It still blocks changes; inspect it from the command line before deciding.
recovery.evidence.closes_itself: It stopped before replacing anything; the next synchronisation on this machine closes it by itself.
recovery.evidence.other_machine: This run belongs to machine {machine}. Close it there; close it here only when that run is certainly over.
recovery.resume.label: Resume
recovery.resume.caption: Closes the journal after verifying the backup still matches; then run the interrupted command again. It re-plans from what is on disk.
recovery.rollback.label: Roll back into
recovery.target.choose: the side each file came from
recovery.rollback.caption: Restores the snapshot this operation created, then closes the journal. Each file goes back to the side it was backed up from; a side needs choosing only for an older restore whose snapshot does not record it.
recovery.dry_first: Check the action first; the button to perform it unlocks after the check succeeds.
recovery.confirm.title: Recover this operation?
recovery.confirm.resume: The journal of {operation_id} will be closed so its command can be run again.
recovery.confirm.rollback: The backup of {operation_id} will be restored into {target}, then the journal closed. Codex must be closed.
recovery.action.NOTHING_TO_ROLL_BACK: Nothing to roll back; journal closed.
first_run.missing.title: No configuration is open
first_run.missing.detail: Open an existing config.toml, wherever it is, or create a new one in a folder you choose. Nothing inside .codex is created or changed.
first_run.exists.title: config.toml already exists
first_run.exists.detail: {path} is in use. You can still create a config at another path; the window switches to it.
first_run.form.title: New configuration
first_run.hint.config: Where the new config.toml goes — any folder you like except inside .codex. Choosing a file that already exists opens it instead.
first_run.config.placeholder: Choose where to create config.toml, or pick an existing one
first_run.config.dialog: config.toml: pick an existing file to open it, or name a new one
first_run.config.required: Say where config.toml should go first.
first_run.hint.machine: Unique and permanent: backups, snapshots and mapping rules on the other machine refer to it.
first_run.hint.codex: Codex's own state directory. It is read and, only during a cold operation, written; never created.
first_run.hint.workspace: A folder your cloud client syncs between machines. Backups, snapshots, plans and logs go under it.
first_run.hint.mirror: Where session files are mirrored. Empty means ${workspace_root}/sync.
first_run.template: The file is written from the template built into CodexSync, with every comment kept. Nothing is downloaded and nothing is created inside .codex.
first_run.workspace.searching: Looking for a workspace this machine already has…
first_run.workspace.not_found: No existing workspace found under a cloud folder. Name one yourself; it will be created when it is first used.
first_run.machine.known: This workspace already has history for: {names}. If this is the same machine (for example, it ran an earlier version), continue it; otherwise pick a new name — two machines under one name mix their snapshots.
first_run.machine.continues: This machine continues the history of {name}: its backups and snapshots stay together.
first_run.after.title: After this
first_run.after.body: Open the Overview and refresh: every check reads the new file. Waiting for the cloud client to finish syncing before a sync on another machine stays your responsibility.
settings.file.detail: Changes are checked by the same loader as the command line, shown as a difference, and saved atomically; the previous version goes to the config history.
settings.no_config.title: There is no config.toml to edit
settings.no_config.detail: Create one on the First run screen.
settings.tab.general.caption: This machine's name and directories. A path may use ${workspace_root}, which stands for the workspace folder.
settings.paths.title: What may be written in a path
settings.paths.help: Substitutions: {substitutions}. A relative path is taken from the workspace root, or from the folder holding config.toml when there is none — here that is {anchor}. Everything else is used as written; ~ means your home folder.
settings.tab.sync.caption: How files are compared, which way a run may write, and what happens on a conflict. Deletions are propagated only if you switch that on, and then only where the previous run proves both sides held the file.
settings.tab.protection.caption: How Codex is detected and how Guardian keeps snapshots. Requiring Codex to be stopped cannot be switched off from the window.
settings.tab.mappings.caption: Directed rules: a path recorded on one machine means another path on another machine. Codex itself does not read these rules; CodexSync uses them to plan repairs.
settings.tab.service.caption: How long backups and logs are kept, where the session store lives, and earlier versions of config.toml.
settings.saved: Saved {path}. Open plans were discarded; scan again before applying anything.
settings.confirm.title: Save config.toml?
settings.confirm.body: {path} will be replaced. Show details to review the difference. Comments and unrelated lines are kept.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.note: Stored with the window, not in config.toml: it changes how CodexSync talks, never what it does.
settings.history.title: Config history
settings.history.caption: Every save keeps the replaced, verified version here, outside .codex, backups and temp.
settings.mapping.example: Example: rule desktop-d, from desktop to laptop, path there D:/Projects, path here C:/Work/Projects.
settings.field.sync.dry_run_default: Command line runs dry by default
settings.choice.sync.delete_policy.propa: delete here when the other side deleted it
settings.reason.sync.session_mode: The latest-date mode can drop branches, so it is readable by plan only: every mutating command refuses a config that sets it, with exit code 4.
settings.reason.sync.mode: Cold sync only: codexSync writes into the Codex state solely while Codex is closed (AI_RULES 2, D-001).
settings.reason.safety.require_codex_sto: Always on: a sync while Codex runs is the failure this tool exists to prevent (AI_RULES 2).
settings.reason.backup.backup_before_ove: Always on: every file a sync replaces is backed up and verified first, so recover can put it back.
settings.reason.safety.fail_on_unknown: Always on: when the state is uncertain, codexSync exits without writing (AI_RULES 3).
settings.hint.sync.direction: A one-way run leaves the other side alone, and records nothing about it: what it skipped stays unsynchronised, so a later two-way run still sees the difference. It also decides a chat changed on both machines: only into the cloud keeps this machine's copy, only into .codex the cloud's.
settings.field.guardian.once_timeout_sec: Give up a snapshot after, s
settings.hint.sync.mode: Always cold: nothing is ever written while Codex runs.
settings.hint.guardian.shrink_ratio: A state that lost at least this share of projects or bindings, and at least the count above, goes to quarantine instead of becoming the latest good snapshot.
settings.hint.guardian.stable_reads: At least 3: the file must read the same several times before it is trusted.
settings.hint.semantic.max_jsonl_line_by: At least 1 MiB. A longer record makes the branch unreadable rather than silently truncated.
settings.hint.sync.time_tolerance_second: Smooths small timestamp differences between file systems.
settings.hint.targets.include_roots: One path per line, relative to .codex and the mirror. Session files, the index, global state and SQLite are handled by the session transfer, not by plain copying.
settings.hint.filters.exclude_globs: One pattern per line, for example **/*.tmp.
settings.hint.sync.delete_policy: Always never: a file deleted on one side is not deleted on the other.
settings.hint.sync.session_mode: Always all: keeping only the last date could discard branches.
settings.hint.safety.require_codex_stopp: Shown for reference. The window never weakens this.
settings.hint.guardian.root_dir: Must stay outside .codex, the mirror, backups and temp.
settings.hint.scheduler.mode: Only safe jobs exist here; writing operations cannot be scheduled.
settings.hint.scheduler.interval_seconds: From 5 minutes; 30 by default. A snapshot every few minutes is rarely needed.
settings.hint.scheduler.jitter_seconds: Spreads runs of two machines apart. 0 turns it off.
settings.hint.scheduler.sync_at_login: A separate task runs one settings sync after sign-in, once the delay above has passed. It is refused while Codex is open, and any conflict stops it before a write. Sessions, restore and repair are never scheduled.
settings.hint.semantic.mirror_compressio: Changing it renames every mirror file and changes the plan id: scan again before applying.
settings.hint.semantic.new_chats: Copy into .codex: a chat this machine never had is written to the path it has on the other machine, as 0.1 did. Codex shows it only if it picks the file up; doctor reports chats it does not list.
settings.hint.conflict.policy: For settings files and chats alike, in every run: the window, the console and the sign-in task. A file counts as newer by its modification time, a chat by its last message; two chats that end at the same moment are still asked about. The copy not kept is saved first: a file in the backup, a chat whole in the conflict bundle.

about.heading: CodexSync {version}
about.what.title: What CodexSync is
about.what.body: CodexSync carries a Codex working state from one machine to another: the projects, which chat belongs to which project, and the full history of every session. It is local-first — it has no server of its own, sends nothing anywhere, and the only copy that leaves this machine is the one you put in your own cloud folder.
about.what.not: It is not a Codex client and not a chat window. It never starts or stops Codex, never reads an account or a token, and never writes to Codex's SQLite databases.
about.rules.title: The rules it works by
about.rule.read.title: Reading is always allowed
about.rule.read.body: Diagnostics, plans and every scan run whether Codex is open or not. A reading taken while Codex is open is marked volatile and cannot be reused by a write.
about.rule.write.title: A write runs only with Codex closed
about.rule.write.body: An undetermined answer counts as running — nothing that changes state is optimistic. The refusal happens inside the core at the moment of the write, against a final check taken immediately before it, so no indicator you saw a minute ago can authorise anything.
about.rule.backup.title: Backup first, and always the same envelope
about.rule.backup.body: A lock nobody else can take, a durable journal, a verified backup of everything that will be replaced, staging on the same volume, one atomic replace, then COMMITTED. A change interrupted halfway leaves evidence the recovery screen can resume or roll back.
about.rule.plan.title: Plan first, then confirm by id
about.rule.plan.body: Every change shows a plan or a dry run and applies only the exact plan id you confirm. The id covers the decisions and the state they were computed from, so if anything moved in between it no longer matches and nothing is written.
about.limits.title: What it leaves to you
about.limits.caption: Each of these is a real limit with a screen behind it, not a disclaimer.
about.limit.cloud: It does not check that your cloud folder has finished syncing or has room. Keeping the handoff order between machines — finish here, let the cloud settle, start there — is yours.
about.limit.registry: Projects also live in Codex's SQLite databases, which codexSync never writes. Moving or remapping a project rewrites the JSON state only; deleting or merging a project is not offered at all.
about.limit.unproven: Where a runtime behaviour has not been observed and written down, the feature that would depend on it refuses instead of guessing. That is why a screen sometimes says a thing cannot be written yet, and says which observation is missing.
about.build.title: This build
about.build.caption: The first thing a bug report needs. Nothing here comes from your Codex state, so it can be pasted as it is.

automation.backup.title: Copies of .codex
automation.backup.caption: A zip copy of the valuable part of .codex: sessions, the archive, the global state, the SQLite catalogues, config.toml, rules, skills and memories. Secrets, caches, logs and temporary files are never copied. A copy is taken only while Codex is closed; a scheduled copy waits until Codex closes. Each copy is verified before it counts, and the oldest is removed only after a newer one is verified.
